title: Reverse engineering a Viking VOIP phone protocol with Claude Code — Boris Starkov, Eleven Labs
talk_summary: Boris Starkov describes using Claude Code to reverse-engineer an undocumented Viking VOIP phone protocol, iterating through port scans, brute-forcing two-letter commands, and building a TCP proxy to intercept traffic from the vendor's Windows software. The key pattern is closed-loop hypothesis testing against a live system, with the human acting as physical hands while the agent orchestrates discovery.

takeaways.what_they_do: The agent proposes a hypothesis, runs an experiment against the live target, observes the result, and refines — repeatedly, without human intellectual input.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it actually like managed to find it and then it confirmed it uh by running uh by running more values through it. So, it it was kind of like closed loop iteration.

takeaways.technique: Brute-force enumeration of an unknown interface
takeaways.what_they_do: When the protocol space was small (two-letter commands), the agent wrote a script to try every combination and classified responses as valid vs error.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it wrote this this program and literally like tried out every single combination of two letters.
takeaways.numbers: 80 valid commands out of the two-letter space

takeaways.technique: Man-in-the-middle proxy to capture ground truth
takeaways.what_they_do: Ran the vendor's working software in a VM behind a logging TCP proxy to capture the exact bytes of a working session, then diffed against failed attempts.
takeaways.evidence_quote: The proxy is relaying it to the Viking phone, but also it logs everything so that to figure out what they're talking about

takeaways.technique: Package solved procedures as reusable skills
takeaways.what_they_do: After cracking the protocol, the agent's findings were distilled into an open-sourced skill so future runs skip the entire discovery phase.
takeaways.evidence_quote: I put all of this as a skill and open sourced it so that now um now everyone if any of you by any chance have a Viking phone

takeaways.technique: Human as physical actuator for the agent
takeaways.what_they_do: The agent orchestrated the whole investigation and issued physical instructions (reboot, listen for beeps) that the human executed, keeping the agent in the driver's seat.
takeaways.evidence_quote: I was actually like the agent for Cloud. Like Cloud was orchestrating the whole thing.

takeaways.what_they_do: Rather than reasoning about the checksum, the agent brute-forced the one-byte value and confirmed it empirically.
takeaways.evidence_quote: checksum turned out to be only uh one byte. So, it's something that you can brute force as well.
